freshness.policy: Change-driven: any newer cited source review invalidates the question snapshot. No calendar-based expiry; re-retrieve and independently review after documentation/taxonomy changes. Fresh is relative to checked-in evidence, not a claim of perpetual correctness.

sources.title: Application card: GitHub Copilot Agents
sources.shortSummary: Agent application card: code-review false positives and missed issues require human investigation; CLI BYOK sends prompts directly to the provider, offline mode disables telemetry and web tools, and invalid provider configuration does not fall back to GitHub-hosted models.

sources.title: Application card: GitHub Copilot Chat
sources.shortSummary: Chat application card: hallucinations and inaccurate code require validation; prompt context is preprocessed for a model. Pull request summaries are on demand, not auto-refreshed, and exclude files with more than 400 combined additions and deletions.

sources.title: About GitHub Copilot CLI
sources.shortSummary: CLI concepts: one-time versus running-session tool approval, allow/deny precedence and git subcommand rules, heuristic trusted-directory scope, non-shell write permissions, and restricted-environment risk mitigation.

sources.title: Using GitHub Copilot CLI
sources.shortSummary: CLI usage: @relative-path supplies file contents; /context reports token usage, /compact compresses history and /cwd changes location. Session-wide tool approval allows options beyond the initial invocation.

sources.title: Content exclusion for GitHub Copilot
sources.shortSummary: Content exclusions ignore specified files but do not apply to symlinks or remote filesystems, and IDE-provided semantic information may still be supplied indirectly. Relevant questions concern supported local IDE inline-suggestion scenarios, not unsupported Agent/Edit modes.

sources.title: Excluding content from GitHub Copilot
sources.shortSummary: Exclusion configuration: enterprise rules cover all enterprise Copilot users and may target Git or non-Git paths; organization rules follow seat assignment. Inherited settings cannot be edited locally, Maintain is view-only, patterns are case-insensitive, and VS Code reloads rules via Developer: Reload Window.

sources.title: Application card: GitHub Copilot inline suggestions
sources.shortSummary: Inline-suggestion application card: suggestions are optional, can be partially accepted, and use cursor code plus open-tab context during input processing. Training data can introduce coding-style biases, and generated code needs review against project requirements.

sources.title: Adding repository custom instructions for GitHub Copilot
sources.shortSummary: Repository guidance: repository-wide and matching path-specific instructions combine; path-specific files use applyTo globs and can exclude code-review or cloud-agent via excludeAgent. Instructions supply guidance, not policy authorization.

sources.title: About Model Context Protocol (MCP)
sources.shortSummary: MCP integrates models with tools and data. Enabling only needed GitHub MCP toolsets improves selection accuracy, reduces errors and frees context tokens; toolsets also include related resources and prompts.

sources.title: Managing GitHub Copilot policies as an individual subscriber
sources.shortSummary: Individual Copilot settings distinguish public-code matching, web search, and AI-training preferences. Individual plans can disable training use; Business and Enterprise data is not used for model training and the individual training control is not shown.

sources.title: Managing policies and features for GitHub Copilot in your organization
sources.shortSummary: Organization owners manage feature policies within enterprise enforcement; an explicitly selected enterprise policy cannot be overridden at organization level.

sources.title: Your first prompt file
sources.shortSummary: Prompt files define task-specific reusable prompts invoked on demand, unlike ongoing custom instructions. The retrieved article explicitly labels prompt files public preview and documents availability in VS Code, Visual Studio and JetBrains IDEs.

sources.title: Prompt engineering for GitHub Copilot Chat
sources.shortSummary: Prompt engineering guidance: state goals and constraints, provide examples, disambiguate libraries and code, decompose large tasks, use tests as examples, iterate and keep conversation history relevant.

sources.title: GitHub Copilot code referencing
sources.shortSummary: Code references for accepted unchanged inline suggestions provide matching source URLs and detected license names. The search covers public GitHub code, not private or non-GitHub code; its periodically refreshed index can omit recent commits. Developer-written or altered suggestions are outside this inline check.

sources.title: Refactoring code with GitHub Copilot
sources.shortSummary: Refactoring preserves behavior. The tutorial recommends understanding code with /explain, extracting focused functions while retaining an original entry-point wrapper for callers, and checking revised behavior.

sources.title: About GitHub Copilot code review
sources.shortSummary: Code-review concepts: organization members without a license need AI credits paid usage plus the unlicensed GitHub.com review policy, and that capability does not extend to IDEs. Customization guidance separates standing AGENTS.md rules from task-specific workflows.

sources.title: Writing tests with GitHub Copilot
sources.shortSummary: Test-generation guidance: supply existing tests for framework consistency, include boundaries and validation failures, mock external services, and separately assert both exceptions and absence of service calls on invalid input.
